subject: SOC 2 Type II: deployment applicability & evidence checklist request
messages:
From: Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@stratusbank.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@auditco.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — questions on which deployment modes are covered for our audit window

Rafael,

Thanks for the call earlier. Our external audit team (Tom copied) is finalizing the scoping for Stratus Bank's 2027 Type II and they need a clear statement of which Redwood-hosted deployment modes can be considered inside the scope of your controls for the audit period 2027-06-01 to 2027-11-30. Specifically:

- We need to know whether Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) are demonstrably within Redwood's SOC 2 boundary for Type II controls.
- For customers on the multi-tenant Hosted API, can any of Redwood's controls be asserted for customer-specific data, or would we need a bridge letter / exception?
- For private VPC deployments (customer-managed networking) — what subset of controls can Redwood still attest to and what evidence can you provide (e.g., network flow diagrams, control ownership matrix)?

Please send a short checklist / memo we can share with our auditors and any draft bridge letter language that would help them evaluate inclusion. If you have artifacts (latest report PDF, a hosting topology diagram, or a draft bridge letter) that would be great.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Zhao
Sr. InfoSec Manager, Stratus Bank
helen.zhao@stratusbank.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

[Attachment: SOC-request-template.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@stratusbank.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@auditco.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — questions on which deployment modes are covered for our audit window

Hi Helen / Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full details below and I attached the latest Type II PDF and a hosting topology (redacted where appropriate):

- Dedicated (reserved pools): In scope for Redwood's SOC 2 Type II — controls over the serving runtime, change management, logging, and tenant isolation applied to dedicated capacity are included.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): the SOC 2 report covers Redwood's platform controls but does not assert per-tenant isolation guarantees for hosted customers; auditors typically accept a bridge letter that maps platform controls to customer applicability and notes the limits of shared tenancy.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: These are hybrid — operational controls implemented by Redwood (e.g., code change, runtime security, incident response) remain in-scope, but network and physical controls are often customer-managed. We can provide a control-ownership matrix and network diagram to show what Redwood attests to.

Action items I will take now:
1) Share SOC 2 Type II latest report (attached).
2) Draft a short bridge-letter template that addresses hosted vs dedicated vs private distinctions (attached as draft).
3) Provide a hosting topology diagram and a control ownership table you can share with auditors.

Kimberly — can you help with the control ownership table and a concise draft paragraph for the bridge letter that explains routing/fallback behavior (cross-pool fallback for burst scenarios)? Marcus / Lauren — any notes on sampling and evidence we should call out for dedicated pools?

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
[Attachment: SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2026.pdf (pdf); Attachment: hosting_topology_v2.png (png)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II — questions on which deployment modes are covered for our audit window

Rafael / team — forwarding Helen's request. Notes for Rafael to include in the bridge-letter draft (high level):

- Dedicated pools: confirm that the customer has exclusive allocation and that we can produce tenant mapping, access logs, change management tickets, and encryption-at-rest config. Sampling window: we can provide sample logs for the audit period by pool id (redacted).
- Hosted (shared): state platform-level controls apply, but per-tenant evidence is limited. Proposed language: "Redwood's Type II report covers the design and operating effectiveness of the Redwood platform. For customers on multi-tenant Hosted API, Redwood can provide platform control descriptions and supporting artifacts, but certain tenant-specific controls (network segmentation of customer-managed VPCs, or customer key custody) are managed by the customer or not applicable to shared tenancy.)"
- Private / VPC: provide control-ownership matrix showing responsibilities; we should attach a diagram and point to the KMS/HSM integration steps.

Marcus — can you pull a short list of evidence items we can promise within 5 business days?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Security Operations
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[Attachment: draft_bridge_paragraphs.txt (txt)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SOC 2 Type II — questions on which deployment modes are covered for our audit window

Quick list of artifacts we can provide for dedicated pools during the requested audit window (2027-06-01 to 2027-11-30):

- Pool allocation manifest (by pool ID) showing customer reservation start/end dates.
- Access control lists and role assignments for admins with change management references.
- Sample audit logs (token issuance, server-side request logs) truncated/redacted per privacy.
- Change management tickets for major runtime updates during the period.
- KV cache and model rollout records that show model pinning for dedicated pools.

Note on routing/fallback: for dedicated pools with burst-to-hosted fallback enabled, we can produce routing policy docs showing the conditions for fallback and the safeguards (e.g., payload isolation, no KV cache bleed, and elevated logging). If Stratus wants absolute assurance of no fallback, they can request a dedicated-only policy and we can include that configuration in the bridge letter.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Helen Zhao <helen.zhao@stratusbank.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@auditco.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — questions on which deployment modes are covered for our audit window

Helen / Tom — attaching the items we discussed: Redwood SOC 2 Type II PDF, a draft bridge-letter with two variants (hosted-acknowledgement language and dedicated-confirmation language), and a redacted hosting topology showing Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private responsibilities.

Summary of the key points to share with auditors:
- Dedicated (reserved pools): in-scope for Redwood's Type II controls. We can provide pool-specific evidence and sampling for the audit window.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): Redwood's platform controls are covered by the Type II report; tenant-specific evidence is limited — we provide platform control artifacts and propose bridge-letter language to clarify applicability.
- Private / VPC / on-prem: controls split — Redwood attests to service-level controls (code, runtime, monitoring), customer attests to network and physical controls. A control ownership matrix is included.

Next steps:
1) Tom — please confirm whether your auditors prefer the dedicated-only bridge or a hybrid paragraph that calls out fallback cases.
2) Helen — if you want, we can prepare a bespoke bridge letter signed by our security lead and include a clause that commits to providing the specific sample artifacts listed by Marcus within five business days after request.

Thanks — attaching draft files now.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
